mutations.because: The collector used to treat any `.log` in a wave directory as a lane, and one session's 442-file root of gate rounds, fix-runner transcripts and probe logs rendered as 113 lanes. Letting a log create a lane again — with no name filter, since the name filter is what hid real lanes — resurrects exactly that behaviour: the fixture that reproduces the owner's root must then yield one phantom lane per file, and the zero-lanes assertion fails.

Any name-based rejection, even one applied to event-named lanes, hides real work: this repository ran genuine lanes named `x13-fix`, `x16-fix2` and `hl5c-fix2`, and a page that drops `x16-fix2` while it runs cannot be asked about it. The fixture that pins the lane's row and attached log fails the moment a suffix rule returns.

Evidence names the lane; the log's whole job is to attach — liveness tail, byte count, mtime — to the lane the evidence already created. An event loop that never looks up `<lane>.log` renders the running lane as silence it cannot date, which is the other half of the rule and fails the same `x16-fix2` fixture from the attach side.

`vanished` must mean something bad — a run that ended or a terminal claim with no PR. A lane whose last words were `started`, with no EXIT and no PR, is a missing measurement, and collapsing this arm back into the old silence-default accuses it of vanishing — the lie that put 102 rows on the page at once.
command: a started event with nothing after it is unknown

mutations.because: A lane's note measures the lane; only the wave header's newest-evidence clock may call a wave past. Restoring the row's old 'past wave' wording resurrects the contradiction the reword removed: in a mixed-age wave — one recent lane, one days-old — the header honestly says live and minutes-fresh while the stale row still prints 'past wave', two statements about the same wave disagreeing on screen. The mixed-age fixture fails the moment the row speaks as the wave again.
